newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy CPI steady in Dec, set to edge up in Jan.
newsitem.headline: Italy CPI steady in Dec, set to edge up in Jan.

text.p: Italian inflation remained steady in December following a year of strong falls, but the price index looks set to edge slightly higher in January for statistical reasons, national statistics office Istat said on Wednesday.
Istat said inflation was 2.6 percent year-on-year last month, unchanged from the November level and in line with forecasts. On a month-on-month basis, prices climbed 0.1 percent in December.
Average annual inflation in 1996 was 3.9 percent compared with 5.4 percent in 1995, meeting the government target.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi wants to get the average annual figure down to 2.5 percent in 1997, but the January data is not expected to get the year off to a sparkling start.
"January last year was a strange month and for this reason the data this January will not be excellent. However in February data will be good," Prodi told reporters on Tuesday.
Istat introduced a new basket of goods to weigh price rises at the start of 1996 and this month will be the first time that the year-on-year rate will be compared to the current basket.
An Istat official said on Wednesday it was "probable" that this would result in an increase in the index although he added that the impact would be slight.
The inflation rate fell strongly last year as both the government and the Bank of Italy put the fight against rising prices at the top of their agendas.
The declining economy and corresponding fall in consumer demand helped the cause, preventing shopkeepers and wholesalers from pumping up their prices.
Price rises in December were muted across all categories of goods, with clothing, education and transport costs showing the strongest gains, up just 0.2 percent by comparison with November.
